in_session_rule: The largest measured burn is NOT cron -- it is interactive session work. Standing rules: (1) NO parallel agent fan-out unless the task genuinely cannot be done sequentially AND the session has headroom -- the 2026-08-11 seven-agent fan-out spent 194k subagent tokens and returned ZERO usable output because the session limit hit mid-run. (2) COMMIT AND PUSH each unit of work immediately: the same restart that killed the fan-out also rolled local HEAD back two commits and destroyed an unpushed commit. (3) miner sweeps report ranked lists, never raw blocked-channel dumps. (4) prefer targeted python one-liners over full-file reads.
law: Cadence is READ off yield, never argued. Safety floors are exempt by construction: a quiet watchdog is a working watchdog.
authority: RECOMMENDS ONLY. ops/crontab.manifest is the authoritative schedule and a human installs it. An advisor that could rewrite the schedule could silently disable an organ nobody knew was load-bearing.

firing_gate.module: libs/ops/owed_work_gate.py, called by ops/run_recommendation_worker.sh before the prompt is built
firing_gate.why_not_event_triggering: firing on every ledger append sounds precise and is strictly WORSE: it starts a session for ONE row and destroys the batching that makes the worker efficient. Eight rows in one session share the repo context, the doctrine prompt and the test run; eight sessions pay all three eight times. The event is 'enough work accumulated to be worth a session' -- a threshold on state, not a hook on a write.
firing_gate.measured_over_provision: the worker drains a BATCH of 8; the ledger is fed ~5 rows/day. Hourly supplied 24 x 8 = 192 row-slots/day against a 5-row refill = 38x. The 113-row backlog hid it -- the existing 'nothing owed' exit never triggered.
fires_on: AGE FLOOR: oldest open row >= 20h (bounds latency; a lone row cannot rot behind a batch that never fills)
LIVE DEFECT: max_audit reporting a live defect -- fires immediately regardless of batch
firing_gate.holds_otherwise: and states its own arithmetic -- how many rows, how old, what would flip it. A silent no is indistinguishable from a broken worker.
firing_gate.fail_open: any unreadable artifact FIRES rather than stalls; a row with an unparseable timestamp is treated as OLD, never new (L1.41).
firing_gate.steady_state_sessions_per_day: ~0.6-1 (simulated over a week of hourly ticks at the measured refill), against 24 ticks/day. The cron tick stays hourly and is now a cheap python stat that exits in milliseconds when gated.
firing_gate.authority: decides only WHEN the drainer runs. Never drops, reprioritises or judges a row; the ledger's disposition rules are untouched.

claude_local_cuts_2026_08_11.note_on_final_figure: 40.3/day was the post-cadence-cut figure with the worker at a flat 24/day. With the firing gate the worker settles to ~1/day in steady state, taking the desk to ~17.3 sessions/day -- an 82% cut from the measured 96.6 baseline. The worker's 24 hourly ticks still happen; they are now a python stat that exits in milliseconds, not a claude session.
